what.deliverable: Free standalone /m:os stock and flow mapper with CLI, MCP server, and MCP Apps view

how.approach: Adopt the mos-brand consumer intake contract as a local workflow record. Apply the selected family architecture, color, typography, identity, and documentation guidance; record product-specific decisions and their source SHAs in docs/BRAND.md. This is a consumer-side record, not a source-repository intake result.

steps.action: Confirm /m:os service naming and distinguish the mapper presentation from the parent family lockup.
Use the exact family palette, bundled type assets, inline SVG, and semantic color and evidence labels.
Check the app, exported UI, accessibility text, and parent logo asset against the recorded source segments.
Record limits and proposed product-family status locally; no source mos-brand repo edits were made.

why.purpose: Give practitioners and students a free, portable way to make system stocks, flows, causal links, evidence status, delays, and unknowns visible.
why.evidence: The deliverable is scoped by this project plan and reviewed against the connected mos-brand source segments listed in docs/BRAND.md.
why.success: The CLI, MCP, and MCP Apps view use the same model; the service is identifiable as /m:os; visual evidence status remains labeled and accessible; no source data is silently asserted.

jtbd.when: A practitioner or student needs to inspect a complex or contested system with an AI client that supports MCP or a local command line.
jtbd.want: I want to express the system context as stocks, flows, causal relationships, delays, assumptions, and unknowns, then see an editable visual map.
jtbd.so: I can discuss boundaries and leverage hypotheses while keeping evidence and uncertainty visible.
